why: All three challenge steps confirm the finding. (1) The quote exists verbatim: hooks.md line 635, the `effort` row of the Common input fields table, ends "The level is also available to hook commands and the Bash tool as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable." (2) The cited code says what was claimed: packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:46-81 builds the hook env with NESSY_EVENT, NESSY_EVENT_DATA, six SAFE_INHERITED_ENV_KEYS and setSanitized field mirrors only — no effort key in any spelling; packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-901 defines SdkAutomationInput with no `effort` member and no index signature, and that object is exactly what hookCommandStdinPayload (hook-command.ts:641-651) serialises to hook stdin. (3) Layer up: both hook execution authorities share that builder and payload (runHookCommand at :664/:737 and the host sandboxed runner at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4344/:4488), plugin runtime env (plugins/data-paths.ts:98-155) adds only PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and the exec-form placeholder list (hook-command.ts:161-170) is closed without EFFORT, so nothing upstream already supplies it. Layer down: a binary-safe `grep -ran EFFORT` over packages/ and apps/ finds effort only in capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136, agent/thinking-levels.ts:70, claude-agent.ts:234 and the codex responses adapter — zero hits in automations/, plugins/hooks-automation.ts or capabilities/runtime-automations.ts. The sibling-subsystem trap does not apply because the claim itself names the sibling correctly (skills): base-agent.ts:2197-2208 threads `effort: this._thinkingLevel` into RuntimeSkillHostContext and THINKING_TO_EFFORT (thinking-levels.ts:70) is the exact documented low|medium|high|xhigh|max vocabulary, so the value exists host-side and is withheld only from hooks. It is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions), and it is not a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference — the fork already implements the same variable for skills citing skills.md:299, so the hook/Bash half is an unimplemented contract. Only defect in the finding is an off-by-one count in its own evidence sentence.
correctedState: `SdkAutomationInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-901) has no `effort` field and no index signature, so the JSON `hookCommandStdinPayload` writes to a hook's stdin never carries `effort.level`. `buildHookCommandEnv` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:46-81) sets NESSY_EVENT, NESSY_EVENT_DATA, six inherited keys (HOME/PATH/SHELL/TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP) and FOURTEEN — not thirteen — NESSY_* field mirrors (:61-74: TOOL_NAME, TOOL_INPUT, TOOL_RESPONSE, ERROR, PROMPT, SOURCE, MODEL, AGENT_ID, AGENT_TYPE, TASK_ID, TASK_SUBJECT, TASK_DESCRIPTION, MESSAGE, TITLE); no NESSY_EFFORT or CLAUDE_EFFORT. Both hook execution authorities are affected — the in-process spawn (hook-command.ts:664, :737) and the host's sandboxed plugin-hook runner (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4344, :4488) — and neither the plugin runtime env (plugins/data-paths.ts:98-155) nor the exec-form placeholder list (hook-command.ts:161-170) supplies it, so `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` inside a hook command or its declared env stays literal. The Bash-tool half of the doc sentence is equally absent: a repo-wide binary-safe grep finds no CLAUDE_EFFORT/NESSY_EFFORT env emission anywhere outside skill-body substitution. The value is fully available host-side: base-agent.ts:2197-2208 supplies `effort: this._thinkingLevel` (withholding only Nessy's undocumented `off`) to skills via SKILL_VARIABLE_SPELLINGS (capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136), and THINKING_TO_EFFORT (agent/thinking-levels.ts:70) already normalises to the documented low|medium|high|xhigh|max vocabulary — the gap is purely that the automations subsystem is never given that host context. Side note for the sweep: a duplicate row of this finding at docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3419-3421 misdescribes the env builder as emitting NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_SESSION_NAME/NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID, which those lines do not do.
